Title: MET Exon 14 Skipping Alterations in Non-Small-Cell Lung Cancer: A Case Report
PMID: 
Authors: 

Abstract
Mesenchymal–epithelial transition factor (MET) exon 14 skipping alterations are rare mutations in non-small-cell lung cancer, associated with high malignancy and poor prognosis. This article presents a case of a patient diagnosed with advanced left upper lung adenocarcinoma characterized by a MET14 skipping mutation. Following first-line treatment with crizotinib, there was a significant reduction in the size of the primary lesion; however, during the course of treatment, an increase in size and prominence of solid components were observed in the right upper lung lesion. A biopsy and subsequent genetic testing revealed an epidermal growth factor receptor L858R mutation in the right upper lung adenocarcinoma, indicating the presence of multiple primary lung cancers. The patient opted against surgical intervention and local treatments, choosing instead a combination therapy regimen that included almonertinib and crizotinib. This treatment approach led to a significant reduction in the size of the right upper lung lesion. The patient’s condition has remained stable without any signs of progression, resulting in an overall survival duration exceeding 53 months.

Case report
A 53-year-old male with a long history of heavy smoking, evidenced by a smoking index of 40 pack-years, presented with the chief complaint that a space occupied in the upper left lung was found during physical examination for 1 month. A chest CT scan conducted at an external hospital on 16 July 2021, revealed a lobulated soft tissue density mass in the upper left lung measuring 68 × 53 mm with unclear boundaries. The mass was closely associated with both the mediastinum and adjacent pleura. Surrounding the mass were several small spots exhibiting increased density and blurred margins. Ground-glass density nodules approximately 8 mm in diameter were identified in the dorsal segment of the right lower lobe, characterized by uniform density and clear borders. In addition, nodules located in the posterior basal segment of the left lower lobe measured about 7 mm in diameter and had broad bases attached to the pleura. Multiple enhanced soft tissue nodules were observed within the mediastinum, with a maximum size of 11 × 8 mm noted. The left pleura exhibited thickening and adhesion; ground-glass nodules measuring 8 × 7 mm were also present in the anterior segment of the right upper lobe.
The patient arrived at our hospital on 25 July 2021. Upon admission, contraindications for puncture biopsy were ruled out. A CT-guided puncture biopsy targeting lesions in the left upper lung was performed on 7 August 2021 (Fig. 1). Postoperative pathological analysis confirmed adenocarcinoma of the left upper lung; immunohistochemical results indicated: CK7 (+), TTF-1 (+), CK5/6 (individual +), P40 (−), ALK(D5F3) (−), ALK-N (−), ALK-P (+), Ki-67 (40%+). A real-time quantitative PCR was employed to detect the METex14. Simultaneously, whole-body bone imaging along with brain MRI and abdominal CT scans showed no significant signs indicative of metastasis. Preliminary diagnosis: left upper lung adenocarcinoma (cT4N2M1a stage IVA METex14) with mediastinal lymph node metastatic cancer and intrapulmonary metastatic cancer. The patient declined chemotherapy and initiated oral targeted therapy using crizotinib.
The patient was regularly monitored, and no significant side effects were observed during the course of treatment. On 20 September 2023, a chest CT scan revealed that compared with the previous scan conducted on 12 February 2023, the lesions in the upper lobe of the left lung had slightly decreased in size (27 × 11 mm, ①). Conversely, the lesions in the anterior segment of the upper lobe of the right lung exhibited an increase in size with a maximum diameter measuring approximately 26 × 10 mm, indicating neoplastic activity. No notable changes were detected in other areas (Fig. 2a–e). Evaluation of curative effect: local progression. To elucidate the mechanism underlying drug resistance, a puncture biopsy was performed on the anterior segment of the right upper lobe of the lung following discussions with the patient and their family regarding potential interventions. The biopsy results confirmed adenocarcinoma in the right upper lung. Immunohistochemistry showed CK7 (+), TTF-1 (+), and P63 (individual +), ALK(D5F3) (−), ALK-N (−), ALK-P (+) and Ki-67 (50%). On 3 November 2023, second-generation sequencing of the lung biopsy tissue identified an EGFR exon 21 missense mutation p.L858R. Upon reviewing the patient’s chest imaging and genetic testing results comprehensively, we considered that the enlarged lesions in the anterior segment of the right upper lung may represent MPLC, while unchanged nodules could also indicate multiprimary malignancies. Final diagnosis: (1) Left upper lung adenocarcinoma (cT4N2M0 Stage IIIB with METex14). (1.1) Mediastinal lymph node metastasis. (2) Right upper lung adenocarcinoma (cT3N0M0 Stage IIB with EGFR L858R mutation). (3) MPLCs? (both lungs). For the left upper lung adenocarcinoma, the overall efficacy evaluation is PR, with a progression-free survival (PFS) of 40 months, and no evidence of disease progression to date. In regard to the right upper lung cancer, the patient declined surgery, radiofrequency ablation, and local radiotherapy options. Following discussions with the patient, targeted therapy consisting of ‘crizotinib 250 mg orally twice daily’ combined with ‘almonertinib 110 mg orally once daily’ was initiated on 9 November 2023. During this treatment period, a significant reduction in the lesion associated with right upper lung disease was observed (Fig. 2a1–e1), resulting in an evaluation of PR for this condition as well. The PFS2 is recorded at 13 months. currently, the patient remains alive without disease progression noted thus far, contributing to overall survival (OS) exceeding 53 months.
